title: Addressable solid–fluid switching that stays put without a sustaining field or settling particles

concept.text: Proposed innovation: a material whose individual regions can be reversibly switched between a freely flowing state and a load-bearing state, then retain the selected state after the switching stimulus is removed. A small, quantitatively specified input would write a mechanical pattern into the material; another input would erase or rewrite it. The target combines local addressability, retention without a sustaining field, stable storage without particle settling, and a flowing state with low resistance to motion.

Magnetorheological fluids provide an existing starting point: they undergo rapid, reversible changes in rheological properties when a magnetic field is applied. The proposed advance adds a demanding combination of retained states, independently controlled neighboring regions and storage stability. The supplied reviews establish relevant limitations of existing suspensions, but do not establish whether this entire combination is absent across all materials.

Conceptual boundary: “solid–fluid switching” here describes a functional transition between flowing and load-bearing behavior. A large yield-stress contrast would not by itself demonstrate a thermodynamic phase transition or a corresponding change in elastic stiffness. Likewise, retaining a material state after removing the field is a different achievement from keeping a magnetic field applied without consuming continuous electrical power.

significance.text: Magnetorheological fluids already have practical uses, including commercial vehicle shock absorbers. Their usefulness nevertheless coexists with sedimentation, off-state viscosity limitations and continuing challenges in balancing storage stability with field-dependent strength. These limitations motivate an advance beyond rapid field-dependent response alone; they do not imply that existing commercial devices are ineffective.

Conditional consequence: achieving the full target would make local flow resistance and load-bearing capacity writable, persistent and rewritable material properties. A forming operation could allow material to flow into a desired configuration and then lock selected regions. Reconfigurable devices could retain spatial patterns of mechanical support between switching events. This would extend programmable rheology from a response maintained by an external condition to a retained pattern within the material.

Conditional limits: practical devices would still require suitable actuation, containment, interfaces and mechanical integration. Programming stiffness would require separate measurements of elastic moduli, because yield stress describes the onset of flow rather than elastic deformation below that onset. Retaining the selected state could eliminate a sustaining stimulus during a holding interval, but would not establish zero energy consumption for switching or for the complete device. Integration into living tissue would additionally require demonstrated safety, biocompatibility and suitable delivery; the supplied evidence does not establish that one further breakthrough would suffice.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability in this proposal is the integration of reversible flow-to-load-bearing switching, material-state retention after stimulus removal, independent spatial addressing and stable storage in one system. It also requires an operational definition of a small stimulus: magnitude, duration and energy must be specified relative to the sample size and intended task. The supplied evidence supports the motivation for this target, while leaving its field-wide novelty unresolved.

For particle-based magnetorheological approaches, the documented barriers include sedimentation driven by the density mismatch between particles and carrier liquid, low off-state viscosity, high on-state yield stress, and long-term chemical and colloidal stability. Durability, particle oxidation and temperature sensitivity also matter. Improving stability while preserving strong field response remains a recurring engineering challenge, although the evidence does not support treating that trade-off as inevitable.

Engineering synthesis: a successful mechanism must hold a selected load-bearing structure after the stimulus disappears, yet release it reliably when commanded to flow. Local addressing must avoid unintentionally switching adjacent regions and must preserve patterns under load and during neighboring writes. Repeated switching must retain the useful contrast without progressive aggregation, irreversible structural change or loss of storage stability. These are requirements of the proposed combined capability, not results established by the supplied reviews.

Material performance must also survive device integration. The 2022 review identifies sealing against leakage, integration with microcontrollers and operation across wider temperature ranges among practical challenges. Solving the material switch alone would therefore leave important work in containment, control and operating reliability.

current_state.text: Established achievements include rapid, reversible magnetic-field-dependent rheological response and commercial magnetorheological shock absorbers for vehicle suspensions. The 2022 review reports that some available fluids provide adequate damping force and response time for particular applications. These achievements demonstrate useful controllable rheology, but do not establish retained material states after field removal or independently writable load-bearing patterns.

S.-B. Choi’s review, published on 3 November 2022, identifies density-mismatch sedimentation as the most serious problem for commercialization of magnetorheological-fluid systems in practical environments and discusses unresolved sedimentation during storage before use. It also reports approaches using nanosized particles and nanosized fumed-silica fillers that improve sedimentation stability without degrading the magnetorheological effect. Consequently, stability and useful field response are not necessarily competing improvements in every formulation.

The Rheologica Acta review by Mousa and coauthors, published on 9 January 2026, identifies sedimentation and off-state viscosity as obstacles to widespread industrial adoption. Its abstract reports partial success with additives, coatings and alternative compositions, while describing stability–yield-stress trade-offs as an ongoing challenge. This supports a qualified account of persistent barriers, rather than a claim that broad industrial use is completely blocked or that every improvement sacrifices another property.

The supplied review’s assessment of the Springer article rests on its abstract and bibliography; the substantive review body and figures were unavailable. Bibliographic references to permanent-magnet and electropermanent-magnet devices do not establish those devices’ performance. For the 2022 article, the supplied review had the full XML text, including tables and figure captions, but did not inspect figure images. No conclusion here depends on those images.

Evidence boundary: neither supplied substantive source text reports the complete proposed combination of latchable switching, sedimentation-free storage and local patterning at device scale. This describes the supplied evidence, not an exhaustive finding about rheology. The supplied bounded search record is empty, so continued field-wide openness through 1 November 2026 is not established. The numerical performance targets below are proposals, not reported achievements.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed integrated demonstration, with thresholds proposed here rather than drawn from an established standard: a centimeter-scale sample switches in under one second between a flowing state with measured yield stress below 10 Pa and a load-bearing state with measured yield stress above 10 kPa. Specify sample geometry, density, temperature and rheometry protocol. Separately demonstrate gravity-driven flow and support of a defined short column, because the yield-stress numbers alone do not establish either behavior for every geometry. Measure off-state viscosity over a specified shear-rate range and compare it with the carrier liquid where one exists; no acceptable carrier-relative viscosity ratio has yet been specified.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed integrated demonstration, with thresholds proposed here rather

completion_criteria.text: Proposed retention and addressing demonstration: each selected state persists for at least one hour after removal of the switching stimulus, including any externally sustained field. Neighboring regions on a proposed millimeter pitch can be written, erased and rewritten independently. Quantify cross-talk, pattern drift and retention while adjacent regions are switched and while the sample experiences a defined load. Report the stimulus magnitude, duration and energy per addressed volume so that the small-stimulus requirement can be evaluated.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed retention and addressing demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed storage and durability demonstration: after 30 days of rest, quantify concentration stratification and compacted sediment using stated detection limits. An absence of compacted sediment alone would not establish sedimentation-free storage. Repeat the switching for 10,000 cycles and show that the specified flowing-state and load-bearing-state contrast, retention and spatial control remain. These tests address documented goals of storage stability, low off-state viscosity, high on-state yield stress and durability, but their numerical thresholds remain proposals.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed storage and durability demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: demonstrate the combined performance on multiple independently prepared samples, disclose the formulation and preparation procedure sufficiently for independent replication, and report failures as well as successful runs. Compare a named commercial magnetorheological damper fluid under the same applicable protocol instead of presuming that it fails. State the demonstrated limits in temperature, load, sample size, addressing pitch, holding time and cycle count. Finite tests establish performance within those conditions and their demonstrated breadth; they do not establish unlimited stability or universal switching behavior.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Proposed claim-specific extensions: any assertion of stiffness programming should include separate elastic-modulus measurements, and any assertion of a thermodynamic phase transition should have evidence beyond a yield-stress change. A tissue-use claim would require its own safety, compatibility and delivery demonstrations. These additional claims need not be prerequisites for demonstrating the core retained, locally addressable rheological switch.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed claim-specific extensions

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: RHE-01, “A constitutive closure that still works in a flow it was not fitted to,” and RHE-02, “A theory of amorphous yielding that predicts the yield stress and whether failure is brittle or ductile,” concern predictive descriptions of material response. Such theories could help characterize switching, yielding and failure in RHE-06. Their central achievements would be predictive laws, whereas RHE-06 requires a material and addressing mechanism that physically realize retained, reversible local states.

Roster-based synthesis: RHE-03, “A continuum law for dense particulate flow from creep to inertia in an arbitrary shape,” overlaps most directly if the switching material uses a dense particle suspension. It could help describe flow and load transmission across operating regimes, but does not itself provide a latch, suppress sedimentation or establish local addressing. RHE-04, “Inverse molecular design of nonlinear polymer-melt rheology,” could supply a design approach if a polymer-based route is pursued; designing a target flow response remains distinct from demonstrating this retained switch.

Roster-based synthesis: RHE-05, “A constitutive theory of active stress that can be inverted for a mechanical task,” shares the ambition of selecting material behavior for a desired mechanical function. Its focus is an invertible theory of active stress. RHE-06 focuses on switching and retaining flowing or load-bearing states after the stimulus is removed; the roster title alone does not establish whether an active-stress implementation would satisfy that retention requirement.

Roster-based synthesis: RHE-07, “The local three-dimensional stress in a flowing material, without assuming the constitutive law,” could provide a complementary way to measure stress distribution, loading and interactions between addressed regions. It is a measurement capability rather than a switching material. The research’s separate reference to historical item 7 as waiting-time-based programmable rheology cannot be identified with this roster entry: its historical source was not supplied, so that claimed overlap remains unverified.

Roster-based synthesis: RHE-08, “A predictive theory of elasto-inertial turbulence and of the drag-reduction ceiling,” and RHE-09, “Computing viscoelastic flow at the elasticity of real processing,” concern prediction or computation of complex flows. They could become relevant to processing or operating a viscoelastic implementation, but neither title specifies retained local switching. RHE-10, “A constitutive law for magma that contains both crystals and bubbles,” addresses a particular multiphase material, while RHE-11, “A topology-based rheology of ring polymers, from pure melts to threaded states,” addresses a particular molecular-topology problem. Their shared subject is rheological behavior; neither should be merged with the functional material capability proposed here.

Conceptual distinction requiring further evidence: the original research contrasts magnetorheological elastomers that change modulus while remaining solid with a bulk material that can flow and then lock. This is a useful way to distinguish stiffness tuning from the target capability, but the supplied substantive evidence does not establish the elastomer comparison. It therefore remains an intended boundary to verify, rather than a documented conclusion about that material class.

change_log.change: Preserved RHE-06, its title and the combined target of local switching, retention after stimulus removal and stable storage.
change_log.reason: The review supports a coherent innovation concept even though the supplied sources do not establish field-wide absence of the combined capability.

change_log.change: Replaced categorical absence claims with findings bounded to the supplied substantive texts and dated sources.
change_log.reason: Two reviews and an empty bounded search record cannot establish continued openness across the field through 1 November 2026.

change_log.change: Distinguished flow and load-bearing behavior from elastic stiffness and thermodynamic phase change.
change_log.reason: Yield stress does not determine elastic modulus or establish a thermodynamic solid–fluid transition.

change_log.change: Separated retention of the material state after field removal from maintaining a magnetic field without continuous electrical power.
change_log.reason: These are different physical achievements; the supplied bibliography does not provide results for permanent-magnet or electropermanent-magnet devices.

change_log.change: Qualified adoption barriers and stability–strength trade-offs, and included the 2022 review’s reports of simultaneous improvements.
change_log.reason: The evidence supports persistent challenges, but not complete prevention of commercial use or an inevitable trade-off in every formulation.

change_log.change: Removed universal claims about bulky hardware and quantified carrier-relative viscosity disadvantage.
change_log.reason: The supplied substantive evidence does not establish hardware size or a general viscosity ratio relative to the carrier liquid.

change_log.change: Retained all proposed numerical demonstration targets and added geometry, rheometry, stimulus-budget, cross-talk and stratification requirements.
change_log.reason: The original thresholds are useful proposals, but need operational definitions and measurements that distinguish gravity-dependent behavior, spatial independence and sedimentation from compaction.

change_log.change: Replaced the asserted failure of commercial damper fluid with a proposed comparison against a named product under the same protocol.
change_log.reason: No supplied result tests a commercial fluid against the complete proposed criteria.

change_log.change: Added reproducibility requirements and explicit operating boundaries.
change_log.reason: Convincing completion requires repeatable combined performance, while finite demonstrations cannot establish unlimited or universal behavior.

change_log.change: Preserved access limitations and differentiated the Springer abstract and bibliography from the available 2022 full XML text.
change_log.reason: The record must not imply access to the Springer review body or inspection of figure images.

change_log.change: Expanded related concepts using the supplied roster and preserved the historical-item and elastomer comparisons as unresolved distinctions.
change_log.reason: The roster supports conceptual comparisons, but neither the historical source nor substantive evidence for the elastomer comparison was supplied.

change_log.change: Qualified tissue integration and device implications as conditional extensions.
change_log.reason: Material switching alone does not establish containment, mechanical integration, safety, biocompatibility or delivery, and the evidence does not show that one additional breakthrough would suffice.

unresolved_issues: Whether any material already achieves the complete combined capability remains unresolved; the supplied evidence does not constitute a field-wide search through 1 November 2026.
The physical mechanism that would combine reversible switching, retention after stimulus removal, local addressing and sedimentation-free storage is unspecified.
A quantitative budget for a small stimulus and an acceptable off-state viscosity relative to the carrier liquid remain to be defined.
The proposed numerical thresholds need an agreed experimental protocol, including geometry, loads, measurement uncertainty and allowable degradation after storage and cycling.
No named commercial magnetorheological fluid has been evaluated against the complete proposed demonstration.
The inaccessible Springer review body may contain relevant detail, but its bibliography cannot establish the performance of the cited devices.
The magnetorheological-elastomer distinction and the identity and behavior of historical item 7 remain unverified from the supplied substantive evidence.
The material’s achievable elastic stiffness, failure behavior and thermodynamic interpretation would require measurements beyond yield stress.
Biological integration remains a separate conditional possibility with unresolved safety, compatibility and delivery requirements.
